public_rationale: Zitron forecasts that TPUs, Trainium/Inferentia, Vera Rubin CPUs, OpenAI's chips and DeepSeek will not make AI cheaper. He means the overall cost of generative AI, not one workload. No deadline is stated. By October 2026 I found price cuts, such as DeepSeek V4 setting off Chinese API discounts, followed by a reported DeepSeek price hike. Prices are not costs. A major lab running TPUs and Trainium does not split its compute by chip, so no cost change can be pinned to a named chip. No decisive event meets the early-resolution rule, so the forecast stays open.
limitations: Overall AI serving costs are poorly disclosed, so it is hard to separate cost from price.
My search of chip-level cost studies was limited.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Neither Google's TPUs, Amazon's Trainium or Inferentia chips, Vera Rubin CPUs, OpenAI's chips nor DeepSeek will make AI cheaper.

statement.excerpt: Google’s TPUs won’t do it, Amazon’s Trainium or Inferentia chips won’t do it, Vera Rubin CPUs won’t do it, OpenAI’s chips won’t do it, and no, DeepSeek won’t do it either.

from_speaker: Amazon's Trainium or Inferentia chips won't do it
Vera Rubin CPUs won't do it
'it' = make AI cheaper (preceded by 'AI is more expensive today than it was three years ago, and it is not getting cheaper')
our_interpretation: 'It' means making generative AI / LLM services cheaper overall, so that the total cost of providing LLM services falls. It does not mean any single workload getting cheaper, and it excludes non-LLM tasks.
No deadline is stated, so the forecast is open-ended.
List-price cuts are not cost reductions unless shown to reflect lower cost.
criteria.support_condition: Would be supported if, over a long period, the overall cost of providing generative AI services did not fall despite wide use of the named chips and DeepSeek. With no deadline, this can only build up over time.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Would be contradicted by credible, documented evidence of a lasting fall in the overall cost of providing LLM services, clearly attributed to one of the named chips or to DeepSeek.

evidence.excerpt: Chinese AI companies are responding with steep API discounts and new billing experiments
evidence.explanation: DeepSeek V4 set off price cuts. Prices are not costs, and the same outlet later reported a planned DeepSeek price hike, so this does not show AI became cheaper to provide.

evidence.excerpt: Anthropic runs a “multi-chip compute architecture across AWS Trainium, Google TPUs, Nvidia GPUs, and AMD GPUs,” without giving any percentage splits
evidence.explanation: A major lab using TPUs and Trainium does not split its compute by chip, so any cost changes cannot be attributed to the named chips.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Filings or independent measurements showing a lasting fall in the overall cost of serving LLM services, attributed to one of the named chips or to DeepSeek. Or evidence over a long period that such costs did not fall despite wide use of these chips.
